subject: Problem compiling tests for stan from source

messages.author: fb1667ba74f25458
messages.subject: Problem compiling tests for stan from source
parts:
Hi,
I am trying to setup a workspace for development on Stan core code. Is there some kind of official guide for this or not? Or a list of requirements? I would prefer to develop on Windows, but if that is going to be too much of a hassle, I can get by with Linux. Here is where I got stuck:
On both Windows 10 + Rtools (gcc 4.9.3) and Debian 8 (gcc 4.9.2), I cannot compile test/unit/mcmc/hmc/hamiltonians/softabs_metric (and a bunch of others, all with the same error)

To be specific, executing
make test/unit/mcmc/hmc/hamiltonians/softabs_metric
yields the error in the attachment (same error on both machines)

Do I need newer gcc or is this some other problem?

On Windows, I also ran into problems with integration tests (https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/2058) but I guess I can live without this.

Thanks
Martin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problem compiling tests for stan from source [Windows compiler?]
parts:
Windows has been a huge pain for us because the toolchain
is a lot more fragile. I'm not sure what our unit tests on
Jenkins are running, but I know they can be run on Windows.

Do the instructions to install CmdStan work? That shouldn't
involve any fvar (that's forward-mode autodiff for higher-order
derivatives). The fvar are required for the Riemannian
metric where it's blowing out in your report.

Our dev ops people are all out until next week, though, so you
may need to wait and try again when they're back on email.
Or maybe someone else knows.

You might be able to get by now avoiding fvar (and anything
in fwd or mix directories).

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problem compiling tests for stan from source [Windows compiler?]
parts:
Hi Martin,

Sorry, there's a bit of misinformation on the wiki (that I didn't know about until I just looked). See this page for how to run the tests:
https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Testing-Stan-using-Gnu-Make-and-Python

(I'll mark the others for removal.)

On Windows, if you have Python installed, you should be able to replace `./runTests.py` with `.\runTests.py` with the arguments the same.

If you wanted to work directly with make, then instead of `make test/unit/mcmc/hmc/hamiltonians/softabs_metric`, you'll have to add the file extension, so: `make test/unit/mcmc/hmc/hamiltonians/softabs_metric.exe`



Daniel

So I guess g++ is currently not supported and I should use clang++?

Best
Martin

parts:
Hi,
sorry I guess I wasn't very clear. I am trying to compile in multiple environments with mixed results. In all cases, I can compile libstanc, but compiling/passing tests is problematic. Maybe it's some misconfiguration on my side, but this is what I get:

a) Windows 10 + Rtools (gcc 4.9.3). I cannot compile some unit tests (see the error attached in my previous email)
b) Windows 10 + Cygwin (gcc 4.9.3) :same as a)
c) Windows 10 + Cygwin (clang++). Can compile tests, but most of them don't pass
d) Debian 8 + gcc 4.9.2 : same as a)
e) Debian 8 + gcc 6.0.3: same as a)
f) Debian 8 + clang++ 3.5.0: all tests compile and all pass except performance tests (which I guess is expected)

So I can definitely do some work on Windows and Debian + clang is totally safe. I am just trying to check whether this is expected.

Hope that clears things up.

Martin

parts:
HI Martin,

I don't see the error attachment (for windows). Could you send that again? 

Regarding seg faults from the compiler: I don't know enough to debug that blind. 1) it shouldn't happen and 2) given that it does, I don't know what's on your system to make that happen.

I've never gotten Cywin to work. But if you have both installed, there might be some sort of library issue. Not sure.

First thing: can you please send over the log file again? I'm not sure where it went. Maybe there's a clue in there somewhere.


Daniel

On Wed, Apr 12, 2017 at 5:35 PM, Martin Cerny <cer...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,
sorry I guess I wasn't very clear. I am trying to compile in multiple environments with mixed results. In all cases, I can compile libstanc, but compiling/passing tests is problematic. Maybe it's some misconfiguration on my side, but this is what I get:

a) Windows 10 + Rtools (gcc 4.9.3). I cannot compile some unit tests (see the error attached in my previous email)
b) Windows 10 + Cygwin (gcc 4.9.3) :same as a)
c) Windows 10 + Cygwin (clang++). Can compile tests, but most of them don't pass
d) Debian 8 + gcc 4.9.2 : same as a)
e) Debian 8 + gcc 6.0.3: same as a)
f) Debian 8 + clang++ 3.5.0: all tests compile and all pass except performance tests (which I guess is expected)

So I can definitely do some work on Windows and Debian + clang is totally safe. I am just trying to check whether this is expected.

Hope that clears things up.

Martin


Dne 12. 4. 2017 17:48 napsal uživatel "Bob Carpenter" <ca...@alias-i.com>:

I'm now confused about what platforms we're talking about.
How did Debian come into the picture?  Stan works with
Linux under g++.

g++ for Windows is what comes with Rtools and what we
generally recommend for Windows users running Stan.

- Bob

> On Apr 12, 2017, at 9:54 AM, Martin Cerny <cer...@gmail.com> wrote:

>

> Best
